    What is asynchronous programming in Python?

    • Asynchronous programming allows only one part of a program to run at a specific time. Consider three functions in a Python program: fn1 (), fn2 (), and fn3 (). In asynchronous programming, if fn1 () is not actively executing (e.g., it's asleep, waiting, or has completed its task), it won't block the entire program.

    What is asyncio in Python?

    • Python’s asyncio provides a framework for writing single-threaded concurrent code using coroutines, event loops, and non-blocking I/O operations. For I/O-bound tasks, async I/O can often outperform multithreading —especially when managing a large number of concurrent tasks—because it avoids the overhead of thread management.
